Bind a package to the Julia library

Source: R/runtime.R
bind.Rd

Call this from the .onLoad() of a package that uses jlbind; use_jlbind() sets that up. The first call loads the compiled library, and each call binds one package's routines to it. If the library is missing or was built from another version of the package, the package isn't bound and its functions give an error; check_backend() says why.

Usage

bind(pkg)

Arguments

pkg

The package name.

Value

Invisibly, TRUE if the package is bound and FALSE if not.

Details

The library is the one from install_backend(), unless JLBIND_LIBRARY names another, or the first package bound was loaded with pkgload::load_all() and has one from build_library().

To run Julia with more threads, set JULIA_NUM_THREADS (a number or "auto") before loading the first package that uses jlbind.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# In a package's R/jlbind.R, as use_jlbind() writes it
.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {
  jlbind::bind(pkgname)
}
} # }
